statement: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Ana eats a quarter of the pizza. How many slices does she eat?

choices.misconception: I found half of the 8 slices instead of a quarter.
I found how many slices are left after Ana eats, not how many she eats.
I added 8 and 4 instead of sharing the 8 slices into 4 equal parts.
I multiplied 8 by 4 instead of sharing the 8 slices into 4 equal parts.

hints: A quarter means one of four equal parts.
Share the 8 slices into 4 equal groups. A quarter of the pizza is one of those groups, so count how many slices are in each group.
Half of 8 is 4, and a quarter is half of a half. Halve 4.

solutions.reliable: A quarter is one of 4 equal parts. Sharing 8 slices into 4 equal groups gives 2 slices in each group, so Ana eats 2 slices. The idea to keep: to find a quarter, share into 4 equal parts and take one part.
solutions.elegant: A quarter is half of a half: half of 8 is 4, and half of 4 is 2.

whyOnTest: Finding a fraction of a small number of things is the first step in fractions, and halving when asked for a quarter is the common slip.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
